summary.text: A 6-year-old girl presented to a dermatology clinic with a 3-month history of an erythematous nodule on the left cheek that began as a single painless, nonpruritic pink papule and grew slowly. She had no constitutional symptoms; examination showed a single firm, shiny, well-demarcated 1.0×0.8 cm nodule with telangiectasia, without ulceration, tenderness, hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

Skin biopsy showed dense dermal infiltrates of small-to-intermediate-sized lymphocytes highlighted by CD3 and CD4, with PD-1 expression by atypical T cells and no significant epidermotropism. Blood tests, peripheral smear, chest radiography, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, and PET were normal and unremarkable, and clinical and histopathological findings confirmed primary cutaneous CD4+ SMPLPD.

Complete surgical excision of the left cheek nodule was performed under general anesthesia by a plastic surgeon. The patient showed full resolution, and no complications or recurrences were found within a 6-month follow-up period.
